content.text: {"id":"00796bfa-e69f-420e-9bf8-292dee6fc957","audio_id":"50b0a46e-0263-404b-8987-ecc7dde8ba0b","status":"complete","created_at":"2026-11-16T07:14:40Z","answer":"The lead is high, childlike and lightly processed, with clearly articulated Korean in the main hook. The chorus moves in connected, lilting lines—“야옹야옹 고양이…” followed by the dog line—rather than isolated word calls; the syllables bounce rhythmically, but neither 고양이 nor 강아지 sounds notably rushed or malformed in the main chorus. The verse shifts to a more spaced call-and-response (“…어디 있니” answered by animal sounds), while the chorus is more continuous and melodic. There is a substantial instrumental break of about nine seconds around 0:34–0:43. The last vocal phrase is followed by a short instrumental resolution; it does not sound clipped. Overall, this recording itself has longer connected melodic phrases and a clear oom-pah/two-beat accompaniment feel; the measured pulse is about 108 BPM in two. I’m describing this recording only, not claiming to have heard the comparison track."}
